channel.title: The Picky Reader — New Releases
channel.description: New and notable theology releases, tracked weekly.

item.title: Salvation — Joel R. Beeke and Nick Thompson
item.description: Ninety family-worship readings from Romans through Philemon.

item.title: Rebels Unraveling — William L. Barney
item.description: William Barney's short political, military, and social history of the Confederacy, arguing that it was a coercive state that began coming apart soon after it was formed.

item.title: Truth Pursuer — Focus on the Family
item.description: A Focus on the Family book exploring creation, science, Scripture, and everyday life, showing how nature and numbers point to God and why Christian beliefs are true.

item.title: Brain vs. Screen — Bethany Barton
item.description: A nonfiction picture book explaining how dopamine and too much screen time affect the brain, and how children can tell when they have had enough.

item.title: The Underground Adventure of the Brave Frog Renée — Mikolaj Pa
item.description: The first Brave Frog Renée book follows a curious frog who packs her supplies and pushes through an oak tree's roots to discover what lies inside the Earth.

item.title: Good Bear, Bad Bear — Hyewon Yum
item.description: A younger sister who feels outshone by her tidy, talented older sister names her teddy Bad Bear, in a story about sibling comparison and self-worth.

item.title: Help! I'm Being Eaten by a Bear! — Neil Sharpson
item.description: A comic guide to what not to do when meeting a bear, from the creators of Don't Trust Fish, illustrated by Dan Santat.

item.title: The Pope Against Nuremberg — Gerald J. Steinacher
item.description: Gerald J. Steinacher uses newly opened Vatican archives to show how Pius XII and Church officials worked against the Nuremberg trials and helped Nazi war criminals escape through ratlines.

item.title: The Accidental World-Slip of Astrid Verity — Jaclyn Moriarty
item.description: A misfired spell drops ten-year-old Astrid out of a tournament and into a Sydney suburb, where a girl named Echo takes her in.

item.title: Backpack, Boy, Berlin — Kip Wilson, illus. Matt Schu
item.description: In 1938, ten-year-old Don moves to Berlin with his diplomat father and begins carrying secret messages for the resistance. A novel in verse.

item.title: The Dogwood Gospel — Cindy Morgan
item.description: Kentucky, 1954. A sixteen-year-old learns she was adopted, runs away dressed as a boy, and joins a traveling carnival as a trick rider.

item.title: The Sedalia Code — Patricia Raybon
item.description: North Carolina, 1943. A teacher at a Black academy decodes a prisoner of war's message about a Nazi plot to kill the president, and when the Army won't listen she acts on it herself.

item.title: Midnight in the House of Commons — Charles Finch
item.description: London, 1881. A member of Parliament is poisoned on the floor of the House of Commons, and Scotland Yard arrests detective Charles Lenox's brother.

item.title: Numb Were the Beadsman's Fingers — Alan Bradley
item.description: A nun dies at Golgotha House and turns out to have lived under a false name. Flavia de Luce and Dogger follow the trail to a crime decades old.

item.title: Matthew — Frederick Dale Bruner, Michael Mears Bruner
item.description: The Bruners comment on Matthew by treating its best-known and some lesser-known passages, drawing on literature, art, music and philosophy alongside biblical scholarship. Frederick Dale Bruner, a mainline Presbyterian scholar, wrote an earlier and widely used Matthew commentary, and this opens a planned four-volume Gospels series.

item.title: The Crusader Storm — Nicholas Morton
item.description: Nicholas Morton's history of the Crusader States from 1097 to Saladin's conquest of Jerusalem, told as a contest among several rival empires rather than a clash of two faiths.

item.title: Ocean of Bones — David Kushner
item.description: David Kushner tells of the Guerrero, a pirate slave ship that wrecked in the Florida Keys in 1827 with 561 Africans aboard, and of the divers searching for the wreck today.

item.title: Castles — Dan Jones
item.description: Dan Jones covers more than three thousand years of fortification, from ancient walls to modern forts, and what castles show about warfare and political power around the world.

item.title: From Age to Age — Keith A. Mathison
item.description: Mathison follows the Bible's teaching on the last things from Genesis to Revelation, treating eschatology as the story of redemption and not only a debate about the millennium. First published in 2009 and now issued in hardcover by Ligonier, it is one of the fuller Reformed treatments of the subject.

item.title: Deacons, Third Edition — Henry Webb & Craig Webb
item.description: The substantially revised third edition of the Baptist standard on deacon ministry, with over 200,000 copies of the earlier editions in circulation. Practical ecclesiology for churches trying to get the office right.

item.title: Tidal Wave — Adam Makos
item.description: The treetop bomber raid on Ploesti, told through four braided lives: an American pilot, a Romanian ace, a princess and a king.

item.title: Readings from the Ancient Near East — Bill T. Arnold & Bryan E. Beyer
item.description: The standard evangelical sourcebook of Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Hittite, and Canaanite texts, in a new generation. Primary sources for anyone who wants to read the Old Testament in its own neighborhood.

item.title: For Us and for Our Salvation — N. Gray Sutanto
item.description: The fourth volume in the We Believe series, working through the doctrine of humanity and sin. Sutanto is among the most careful of the younger Reformed dogmaticians, and this is anthropology done in the Bavinck line.

item.title: Ezra-Nehemiah — Gary Edward Schnittjer
item.description: Schnittjer's technical commentary on the return from exile, reading Yahweh's faithfulness against the persistent unfaithfulness of the people he brings home. Substantial enough for the study, clear enough for the pulpit.

item.title: Reading the Reformation — Zachary Purvis
item.description: The Reformation as a reading revolution — the printers, scribes, and theologians who put books in ordinary hands and changed what Christians could know.

item.title: Frontier Faith — Brandon J. Crawford
item.description: Edwards's years among the Stockbridge Indians, a readable slice of his missionary life and thought.

item.title: Prodigal Culture — Andrew T. Walker
item.description: Examining 10 personal, social, and existential crises affecting men and women today, Andrew T. Walker explains why the Christian moral tradition is the remedy to social decline.

item.title: Scroll Less, Live More — Samuel D. James
item.description: Scroll Less, Live More offers 10 practical habits for navigating the world of technology, helping teens keep digital tools in their proper place and find wisdom in God's perfect design.

item.title: The Declaration of Independence — Michael D. Hattem
item.description: Michael Hattem's brief history of the Declaration across 250 years: how it went from an announcement to a national symbol, and how later movements have claimed it. 144 pages.

item.title: The Lord Is My Light — Trevin Wax
item.description: Wax arranges a liturgy for daily prayer, pairing Scripture readings with prayers and confessions drawn from Christians across the centuries. An evangelical daily office for readers who want structure without leaving their tradition.
